Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can Some Augason Farms stuff I buy as emergency food, some I buy for regular use. If I can price out something in this form that is same price or less than other forms, then I go with this as it can be stored away or kept in my working pantry. I use a lot of Augason Farms, and I've been pleased with this.

Dehydrated celery is a great addition to the pantry. Sometimes I dont have fresh, or I have fresh that went bad, or I dont find it in the store, or what is there looks bad, or price is way outside my budget. Having some dried celery tucked away in my pantry really helps stretch the budget and brings value to my time.

I keep the recipe trifecta on hand, "mire poix": celery, carrot, and onion. I keep fresh, frozen, and dried on hand. Usually used in recipes that will help rehydrate these foods no problem. Celery is very easy to rehydrate. I usually just add to the cooking process and its good to go.

Food scarcity is legit, so if you can stock up when items are on sale, then I recommend to do so. Consider it insurance.

FYI: food and such are sold based on weight, not volume. There is 1lb, 2 oz packed in this #10 can (that reads, "number ten" not "ten pound"- it is a size of can). Using a #10 can means that it provides uniformity among storage. Emergency supplies are packed for long term and are packed to stack. They also float. They can be repurposed. Even if one gets a dent, contents are still good (unless and actual hole, which is not likely to happen). The food will not be filled to the brim, and also.. food settles after packing.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can

Gaiam Yoga Mat - Easy Roll 6mm Exercise & Fitness Mat Perforated Easy Rollup Edge for All Types of Yoga, Pilates & Floor Exercises (68" x 24" x 6mm Thick) This is a high quality yoga mat which, with a depth of 6 mm, is much thicker than the average yoga mat, a real plus for comfort. The "sticky" surface lacks any tendency to get slick when dampened by perspiration, which helps prevent an accidental sliding fall. This same surface also has the ability to cling to itself, not nearly as much as Velcro does, but enough to help hold the mat securely in place after it is rolled up.

This mat is made of PVC, and PVC definitely outgasses toxic fumes. If you have somewhere you can air out this mat for a few days, such as a porch, it would help speed up the process of dissipating the toxic fumes. This type of PVC is a flexible material which is amenable to bending due to being made with plasticizers like phthalates (e.g. diisononyl phthalate or DINP). Phthalates are part of a family of industrial chemicals used not only to soften PVC plastic, as in the case of this mat, but also as solvents in cosmetics and many other consumer products. Ingesting phthalates transdermally or breathing in their fumes can, over time, cause damage the liver, kidneys, lungs, and reproductive system. Fortunately a product like this will eventually cease to outgas, but utilizing cosmetics containing phthalates on a regular basis is a much more serious risk of health damage.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Yoga Mat - Easy Roll 6mm Exercise & Fitness Mat Perforated Easy Rollup Edge for All Types of Yoga, Pilates & Floor Exercises (68" x 24" x 6mm Thick)

Total Gym XLS Men/Women Universal Total Body Training Home Gym Workout Machine with Squat Stand, Leg Pull, 2 Ankle Cuffs, and Exercise Chart I just wanted to clear this up, this is the same exact package that is sold by Total Gym Direct! The only difference is that TG Direct offers the AbCrunch as a bonus, but their package is more expensive and you can purchase the Abcrunch on Amazon and still be way below the cost of purchasing the package from TG! I ordered the Abcrunch, which comes with a DVD, and the Weight Bar and still paid way below the 60% off price of TG Direct. I would say to wait until you get your TG before purchasing any attachments because I received a promo code with my TG for $20 and $30 off for accessories to use on the TotalGymCatalog dot com. This Total Gym came with 5 DVDs (workouts at every level and includes a pilates dvd), the Pilates package, wall chart, training deck and holder, wing attachment. Everything you need to workout!

There is no assembly, it comes fully assembled. I do recommend watching the set up dvd so you do not hurt yourself setting this up and you fully understand how it folds and unfolds. I did my first workout yesterday and I really feel it today. This machine is as smooth as butter! It is very quiet and appears to be of good solid quality. I bought a lesser quality type machine similar to this years ago and the difference is like night and day. My boyfriend is 6'4 and has no problems working out on this machine. The bench is almost 47" long x 16" wide and most of the exercises are done with your legs either bent up and crossed or sitting on your legs or with them hanging to the sides of the bench. This machine is 90" long and even doing squats there is still plenty of room.

The workouts are fun to do and don't take that much time. I was shocked how fast time went by as I was working out. That is what keeps people motivated. The workout never felt redundant. I feel fortunate to have a room dedicated to working out because it is not a small machine and I will leave it unfolded. In a small apartment this might feel like an elephant sitting in the room, but if you are willing to fold it up after each workout, it folds up very compactly.
Another bonus, if you have amazon prime you receive this machine in 2 days of ordering it!!! Whereas, the TG Direct site may take 10days! I am very happy with my purchase and will update if I notice any changes with this machine.
If you are looking for a less expensive Total Gym you might want to check out the Total Gym 1800 Club package. It is 399. and comes with many of the same equipment as this package. I just happen to come across it on youtube. In fact, watching the video, it looked as if it came with the AbCrunch. It is worth checking out if this package is not in your budget. Now that I have the XLS, I do not see much of a difference between the two machines except for the price and change in the bench style. There may be other differences, but it looks to be very similar and at a much lower price!
Update 7/27/2012 - I have been using the TG every other day with the beginning DVD and LOVING it!! I get really excited about working out now. Using the DVD is truly like having a personal trainer and I really sweat with the workout. I am so happy that I made this purchase and would recommend to anyone at any level wanting to get in shape. It gives a great cardio and toning/strengthening workout! At first I was a little worried I wasn't going to be able to keep up, but I just kept doing the best I could and now I love it and can't wait to work out. On days that I am not on the TG, I work out on my recumbent bike and am amazed how I feel now just in this short time. Sometimes I use the TG and the Bike on the same day and am working on doing that more.
text_fidelity_b: Total Gym XLS Men/Women Universal Total Body Training Home Gym Workout Machine with Squat Stand, Leg Pull, 2 Ankle Cuffs, and Exercise Chart

text_fidelity_a:
JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes The UPS deliveryman carried this box to the front door with ease, but I quickly learned that a 108 lb., smooth, cardboard box is NOT that easy to maneuver. So just be aware this is a heavy shipment!

I was worried this was going to be a cheap and flimsy bike, but that's not the case in any way! This thing is welded, heavy gauge steel with a thick paint job (probably not powder coated). The handles are equally solid with a thick rubber grip, probably hot dipped. Basically, no amount of sweaty hands are going to cause the grip to deteriorate. The mechanics are practically silent.

Assembly is a cinch. There are 4 bolts used to attach the feet, three adjustable handles to attach the seat and handle, and two pedals to screw on. All of the required tools are in the box.

I've only ridden on it once, but the seat is soft (not that it matters if you're standing). The electronic display is of utmost cheapness, though. I was afraid that I was going to break it when installing the (included) AA batteries. It provides very basic information such as time, distance, "speed", and "calories" but there is no input for height and weight.

I'm waiting on a cadence sensor that will attach to one of the crank arms, and plan to use that with an app to get better feedback on pace. I also downloaded the Peloton app (30 day free trial) and was able to follow along just fine with the beginners ride. The resistance knob doesn't have a numeric scale (just +/-) so you'll have to judge for yourself based on how it feels.

Final thought is regarding the maneuverability. The front wheels are a bit small and made of a hard plastic so it will be hard to roll across carpet. You can tell from the photo we have a hard floor, and if it gets caught on debris, it may easily get stuck or scratch the floor.

Overall, I'm impressed with the build quality, assembly and performance. Only negatives are the ultra cheap display, lack of any integrated wireless technology (BYO), and the small wheels to move it around.
text_fidelity_b: JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Strider Foldable Treadmill, 20-Inch Wide Running Belt with Optional Exclusive SunnyFit™ App and Enhanced Bluetooth Connectivity I should start by saying when I first got this treadmill it was for a Christmas present so I was very happy with it. I am an avid runner and in the winter months I hate being inside without being able to run and a treadmill is a life saver.

When I first started running on the treadmill it was good, although the belt was a little narrow. After about two weeks the motor just randomly stopped while I was running and shut the whole treadmill off.

I spoke to their technical support team and they said I needed to lubricate it which I was doing regularly. I went back and forth with them until finally they sent a new motor. I installed the motor myself of course, and within 2 weeks the same problem was happening.

I decided to tighten the motor a little bit to the belt which ended up helping the issue. At that point I limited my speed on the treadmill in hopes to keep it going, because I still needed to run. After another 2-3 weeks the belt would barely move at highest speeds. I would set it to 7mph and it was at walking speeds.

This continued for a few weeks and then I tightened the motor again. After a month or two of trial and error, tightening motors, etc. the treadmill finally stopped going faster than a walk at all. Today, I just opened the treadmill up and it looks like the motor mounts bent. There is no way to repair it. After all of the headache and trouble, and dealing with not being able to run on long run days, I've decided to give up and purchase a new treadmill from a reputable brand. I would suggest you do the same.

Unfortunately, because I got strung along by their support, I am no longer within my window to get a refund so I guess $600 lost. Please do yourself a favor and find something that will work that is reputable, these off brands suck.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Strider Foldable Treadmill, 20-Inch Wide Running Belt with Optional Exclusive SunnyFit™ App and Enhanced Bluetooth Connectivity

I was also curious about "seamless" leggings as my wife has some sensory issues when it comes to clothes. They are a beautiful light lilac color. These leggings appear to high quality. The material is not thin, nor too sheer.

They are very stretchy, yet nicely elastic that they fit well and hold their shape. My wife did struggle a bit getting them over her feet as they are reinforced and tapered at the ankle, but once on they they fit her ankles well. The fabric does not quite have the same feel as other yoga pants that have a more "spandex" feel. These have a bit more cotton feel to them. Which is odd because they are a polyester - spandex mix. They do not have side seams but they do have inner seams on the legs. You can definitely tell when they are on that they are seamed. The backside does have two moon shaped designs under each buttock, which maybe for additional support. Although my wife is not sure that she will wear them out of the house because it looks a bit odd. The high waist is also reinforced, but does roll down, which can be annoying.

Overall, depending on your tastes, these feel like a good quality legging. My wife however, isn't a big fan of their aesthetic look but will definitely wear them to sleep or lounge around the house in.

text_fidelity_a:
Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel I bought two of these and both were non-functional, out of the box.

On the first one, the included line was tangled around inside the mechanism. I had to take it apart and unravel about 6 feet of line that was all caught up in the case. It's hard to explain, but it was basically wedged between the outer casing and the internal components, not just in the spool itself.

On the second one, the casting button was completely unseated on one side. The button has two small pegs which pivot inside of holes in the steel case. I had to take the bottom of the case off, bend the steel tabs that hold the pegs in place, reseat the button and bend the tabs back.

Both work great now and all the components seem pretty good, but this company has some serious quality control issues with assembly. It is pretty ridiculous that 2 out of 2 that I ordered were DOA, still sealed in the undamaged factory box. Luckily, I knew how to fix them, but most people who aren't mechanically inclined or perhaps know very little about reels would have had to return both of them. That is really unacceptable.

Still, they are great little reels now and they would be 5 star if not for the time I had to spend on fixing them. If you have some tools and are confident about taking things apart, I wouldn't hesitate to buy one. If not, well, you might be rolling the dice.
text_fidelity_b: Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel

--Wooden handle is smooth and comfortable; I like it over straight handles. I feel like I can get a good grip. Very important consideration depending on conditions/elements, if hands are cold, etc.

--Tin of fire putty with secure twist off cap (legit good product). Good size. They dont skimp.

--whistle is attached via key ring to the drawstring portion of the storage bag. Can be taken off and placed elsewhere.
--Orange drawstring bag with reflective strip on one side
--Ferro rod, multi tool/striker is tethered together via a length of paracord
--separate bundle of paracord
-- I have something not shown: A retractable metal bellow (a straw of the sort for feeding oxygen to a spark or established fire). The style of this reminds me of a retractable antenna. Seriously – you could guide ships through a dense fog with this light. It’s bright with a capital B!

That’s not a bad thing. On a dark rural road or trail when there are no streetlights, this lamp will literally turn night into day. However, it can be a problem in more populated areas or when there are oncoming cars. If this is not positioned properly with the light beam facing down, you will completely blind anyone coming in the opposite direction. This is a light you need to use with caution when around others.

The build quality throughout is excellent. The light body is all metal and very sturdy. There are a lot of cooling fins in the body to help dissipate heat. Still, even with the fins, this gets very hot after it’s been on for a while.

The light attaches to the handle bars via rubber rings that slip over two mounting brackets. If properly positioned they hold the lamp tight, but you do need to fiddle with the rubber rings a bit to ensure a tight fit. While a permanent mounting option would be nice, I can see the advantage of the rubber rings since it makes putting the lamp on or taking it off a tool-less process.

The battery pack connects to the lamp with a stout cord that also has a screw on jacket to keep everything attached while riding. The battery pack itself has a rubberized coating plus a rubber jacket to keep it weather tight. It stows in a thick nylon pouch with sturdy Velcro closures and straps to keep it closed up and attached to the bike. Given all that protection, I have zero concerns about water splashing on the battery causing any problems.

The cord between the battery and the battery pack is a little over 30 inches long which proved to be ample for me to put the lamp on the handle bars and the power pack on the front fork.

It’s very simple to use – only one button which is located on the back of the lamp. Press it once, and it turns on the full set of 7 lamps. Press it again and only the middle three lamps are lit (which is still very bright). Press it a third time and it starts to strobe on/off (all 7 bulbs). One more press and it turns off.

It is VERY annoying that you can’t go from ON to OFF without going through the strobe mode.

It includes a wall charger to recharge the battery pack. The stated battery life is 4 hours at full power which proved to be pretty accurate. The battery is rated as 7800mAh, which is impressive. What is not impressive is the battery life indicator – it’s located on the charger, rather than the device. So, to determine how much battery life is left you have to disconnect the lamp, connect the battery to the charger, and look at the LED on the charger. Plus, it only has two colors – green means 30% to 100% capacity left; red means less than 30%. Not exactly helpful in use.

Another miss is the manual – it literally is missing. No documentation at all came in the box. Granted, this is a pretty easy device to figure out, but at this price point a manual or instruction sheet of some type really should be included.

Although the negatives concerning the user interface and manual temp me to drop this to 4 stars, I’ll keep the rating at 5 stars for two main reasons: build quality and performance. This truly is the most powerful light I’ve ever used, equaling the performance of a car’s headlamp. Provided that this is used properly to avoid blinding oncoming traffic/bicyclists, it is a huge benefit at night especially on a trail. Due to the power of it, however, I would NOT recommend it for urban/suburban street use since the risk of harm to others is just too high.

AKSOUL Self-Inflating Camping Pad Sleeping Mat - Ultralight Camp Air Mattress Pad Connectable 2 Wide Extra Thick Sleep Pads with Inflatable Pump for 2 Person Durable Compact for Backpacking Hiking My partner and I are elderly, live in hot/humid Georgia, and all the windows in our rental house are painted shut. If we were to experience a blackout here, we would die. After the "What did our grandparents do when they didn't have air conditioning" conversation, we realized that having a few well-ventilated pop-up tent "bedrooms" outside would mimic the screened porches where people used to sleep when it was too hot inside the house. We sleep in separate bedrooms, so two tents will provide ample room for each of us to be comfortable and also not freak out the dogs who insist on sleeping with one or the other of us.

So I ordered the tents and two of these self-inflating double sleeping mats. With waterproof garden tarps I already have under the tents plus a solar panel/generator setup to power laptops, phones, and fans, I think we might be able to survive a blackout. Fortunately, we do have a few shady areas in our back yard where we can pitch our tent rooms. And if we have to evacuate, we can throw our kit into the back of our truck along with our solar oven and kelly kettle.

This sleeping pad is not going to be nearly as comfortable as a real bed, but I think it will be better than nothing. Also, in case of tornado warnings (which we also get), we can use these mats to cover ourselves if we have to hunker down in the bathtub. At our age, regular mattresses are a little hard for us to lift and move. Better to have a plan than to be impotently frightened of climate volatility.

text_fidelity_a:
Giro Section Adult Dirt Cycling Helmet I agree with some of the other comments that this helmet looks much bigger in person than it does in the photos. Sportier helmets don't come down so far on the sides and are also tapered at the edges so that they look smaller. This helmet is one thickness all the way from the top to the edges, so you can see that you've got a full inch of plastic and foam surrounding your head all the way around. I've never worn an Army helmet, but I'm guessing that this one looks pretty much like an Army helmet when it is on your head.

On the plus side, this helmet is surprisingly lightweight. The sticker inside my size large helmet says 325 grams and it actually weighs less than my high-end road racing helmet (which is full of big ventilation holes).

Sizing is similar to sportier Giro helmets. My size 7 5/8 head fits in this helmet comfortably, but larger heads may have a hard time. I can't wear some other models of helmets because they don't come in a big enough size, but this one is no problem.

I bought this helmet to for commuting bad weather. The lack of vents will keep my heat in and the rain out. In hot weather, especially with long hill climbs, I'm going to use something with much better ventilation.

If I had paid full list price, I would be disappointed in this helmet because of the huge size. For half price, I'll live with it for commuting. The large flat surfaces will probably be good for sticking on lights.
text_fidelity_b: Giro Section Adult Dirt Cycling Helmet

text_fidelity_a: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu I quite like this bottle.  I bought this in the 16 oz size and i maybe should have gone larger, as i really like the design.  I use this one for coffee, though If it were larger i would keep water in it.  The thing I like about this over others in the Kleen Kanteen range is the lip and threading.  The classic bottles have threading on the outside of the lip of the bottle with a cap which screws over the lip, clamping its edge against a gasket.  I have come to find this design prone to leaks if the gasket isn't properly seated.  The TKWide range just doesn't have this problem.  The threading is on the inside, low, under the lip of the bottle and the cap screws into it with a simple o ring.  I'm not a huge fan of the "cafe cap" but i just remove it and drink from the lip of the bottle which is itself quite comfortable.  It's kleer that kleen kanteen designed this bottle to work in exactly this way, as the lip of the bottle is the most comfortable of any i've ever encountered to drink from and they even make an assortment of different caps for this line with different features.  I'm considering getting the simple steel loop or bamboo cap to eliminate all remaining unnecessary parts.  The user experience drinking from the bottle with cap removed is similar to drinking from a tall glass tumbler.  The threading is recessed from the lip and doesn't interfere with drinking at all.. I also like that the 'cafe cap' is easily disassembled.. I hate cleaning these things, once a few weeks of coffee residue gets on them.  I've dropped this bottle twice and it has a dent now, but nothing severe.  I find it well made and well engineered and though, in my head at least, this bottle rivals the yeti ramblers which are similar, its about half of the price or less.
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu

Streamlight 69300 TLR-1 Series and & TLR-2 Glock Style Contour Remote, Black ORIGINAL REVIEW: This DOES fit a G21 Gen4 setup. When I got the package it states that it won't fit the TLR-2G. My goodness, why couldn't this info be shared during the product description here or the manufacturers website? I really needed this to work because my TLR-2G doesn't stay activated after a few rounds of fire with the regular cumbersome reach and toggle switch.

UPDATE 07/28/14: After having to sell my TLR-2G, I picked up the standard red-laser TLR-2HL. The directions are a little lacking but I was able to figure it out. Fit is very tight, but that is how you want it so the switch doesn't fly off during use.

TIPS: The push pin for the original battery door will need to be removed. If you are looking into the battery compartment, you will be pushing the RIGHT end of the pin towards the left. Once you have about an 1/8 inch of exposed pin, you will need to use some needle-nosed pliers to pull it out the rest of the way. Save the pin for later use just in case.

Here is where the included directions are a little lacking. The thin metal 1/4 inch wide clamp that held the original door down is NOT to be removed. You will be using that same clamp to clamp down the new hinge-less remote. It took me a few minutes to realize this. I was getting ready to take the clamp completely off via another push pin. I'm glad I didn't. Now, loosen the rail clamp on the light as wide as you can, trust me on this. Insert the trigger end first, then the light's rail clamp to your Glock's rail.

Single press and it lights up. Double tap and you get strobe. At least that what seemed to be working for me.

Like another reviewer shared, ff you have big hands, yes, you will notice that your fingers are slightly off natural position. This is a trade-off I'm willing to make so that I am not toggling with the original switch with my off hand. I am not a LEO, this is strictly for home defense use. I'd rather keep my off hand supporting my shooting hand or holding an extra mag if needed.
text_fidelity_b: Streamlight 69300 TLR-1 Series and & TLR-2 Glock Style Contour Remote, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Plano Stowaway Micro Organizer Premium Tackle Organization I don't know why everybody is having problems with these 3214 boxes. I've been using them for years - at least 10 years - the brownish kind that's labeled "Micro Mag". I've never had a single problem with them and I prefer them over the 3414 soft plastic white ones, although these are slightly heavier than the 3414's. When I want to just carry one little kit in my vest or pocket, these are perfect. I've accidentally dropped them on hard surfaces without any breakage or cracks. Of course, I'm sure there's a limit to how much abuse they will take, but if you're careful with your fishing gear there should be no problem.

Since I gave two of them away to my son and wife, I needed a replacement. I tried to consolidate all of my trout gear into one, but found I could be a little more organized with two. I use one for all my terminal tackle, hooks and weights (separated by size) and I'll use the other one for all my lures. The problem I have with the white 3414 box is that the lids don't seal tightly. Every one I've ever had or inspected on the shelf has the same issue. The lids are slightly bowed out. So, when you put a bunch of tiny #14 hooks, swivels, and the like, they always end up migrating to another section. Really irritating. That NEVER happens with the hard 3214.

When I saw these green ones (I've never seen them in the stores), I thought it was perfect. I like the color and it differentiates between my brown one. Comparing it to my old brown one, it is exactly the same - except mine is not labeled Micro Mag like in the picture. The top is just kind of plain with a small Plano logo. I actually prefer this because it makes seeing the contents easier.

As far as all the complaints with the latches not catching, I have NO idea what that's all about. text_fidelity_a:
Misfit Shine - Activity and Sleep Monitor I am posting a "reserved" review...After the experience buying the black one for my husband and the first one arrived, opened and not working! (BAD Amazon order fufillers sending an obviously opened and non-functioning product) I have had my Shine for about a week... I wear in on my wrist most of the time.. I chose to remove it before bathing. If I were swimming I would leave it on, although the propoganda states that if you wear in "treated" water it reduce it's life - odd to me. Also, it doesn't auto sync. You must sync it to your phone each day. The upside is that you don't have to charge it, just replace the battery. It seems to be fairly accurate. I will update if there are any use/wear issues. It arrived quickly (I have prime) and in good condition.

UPDATE 10/15/2014..... So... I've been using the Shine for about a month... it hasn't failed, to my knowledge. It syncs when prompted to, although I have found sometimes it takes longer than others even though I set it right next to my phone each time. It has survived one system "update" without noticeable issues. I chose to remove it when bathing. I do wish it auto synced rather than to manually prompt it to do so every morning. I have learned that if you are interested in following your sleep pattern one night at a time (it doesn't provide a graph of experience, however you can review night by night - would be nice to have an over all view), you must use the wrist band. Using the magnetic clip does not provide sleep info. Also note: when using the magnetic clip, be aware that it is HIGHLY likely to detach from you and attach to something else magnetic if it gets close and you may not even notice that you've left your Shine on something else. The "watch" band seems to be very durable. The time option of the Shine is interesting and maybe entertaining for a short while, however, it is not as "obvious" as you might think. It is very easy to misread. I found myself double-checking my phone a lot because I would think... hmm... my Shine says 5:30 but I KNOW it's 6:30. I eventually chose to "turn off" the watch function. Which is another thing.. to change anything you must be attached to where ever you downloaded the progam, not an option on the Shine itself. All of this is just information for those of you who are researching options. Honestly, the best part of the Shine for me is the battery and not having to charge it each night or every few nights. I didn't think I would mind the wrist band, but I am bored with it and it's look now, which sometimes interfers with my jewelry options. I considered the necklace accessory, however, the reviews of it were overwhelming not so great, so I stuck with the wrist band and the clip that comes with it. Over all it seems to fairly accurately record movement. However, when this one fails, I am probably going to search out the next option unless they do the subtle upgrades mentioned above... but even then, I think I'm still looking for the device that works best for me. Hope this info helps you in your research!
UPDATE: NOV 18 2014.... Sooo...about 2 months in and now it sometimes doesn't sync the sleep info. Randomly it just fails. And it would be nice if it would provide a graph or chart or some analysis of your sleep and workout info... but nope. It does now sync with My fitness pal, which is a free easy way of keeping track of your food/calories. Honestly, it's still disappointing because there are so many others that offer you more for about the same amount of money.

UPDATE: 12/4/2014.... Ok... the shine has officially stopped syncing... it's been "sputtering"... not recording data... taking a really long time to sync... etc.. I tried replacing the battery just in case. So... in less than 3 months.. it has stopped working. I would NOT recommend this pedometer at all. You would like to think it work for at least a year! I have the first gen fit bit... I just wanted one I could wear on my wrist. Honestly, I think I will try the wrist model of the fitbit.
text_fidelity_b: Misfit Shine - Activity and Sleep Monitor

Senyoo IP68 Waterproof Portable Camping Lamp and Rechargeable Emergency Light This was somebody's good idea, and I like it. We all have too many little handy gadgets that make our lives easier while also proliferating USB cables like rabbits and, in aggregate, taking up a lot of space.

The idea of making a lantern that also is a power bank for charging or running USB-compatible devices is GREAT. Why would you take both a lantern and a separate power bank along with you if you don't have to? If everyone on your trip has one of these as a personal light for hiking trails, there will be a lot of juice among you!

This lantern on the power-saving (dimmer) white light setting is gracious plenty light to read by, at least for me, and the bright light is quite good for seeing in the dark while on a trail. You can carry it as a light stick or stand it up on its charging end; the two USB ports, one standard, one mini, are tucked inside a screw-on cap that keeps it all waterproof until you take the cap off. On the on/off end (the green button as shown), there is a convenient wire hanging loop plus a lanyard (I received two) for looping it onto a belt, tactical bag, or tent loop. The red strobing lights serve as emergency lights. One of them flashes in a particular fast/slow sequence that reminds me of Morse code, so I wonder if it's not flashing a specific SOS-type signal. (Senyoo, can you clarify?)

The only thing I wish this had that it doesn't is a way to stow its USB charging cable. Throw in an alarm clock—or an ear-splitting alarm for the night joggers among us in case we are attacked—and this would truly be the Swiss army knife of lanterns. But it's already pretty great as it is. I was given this product in exchange for my unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: Senyoo IP68 Waterproof Portable Camping Lamp and Rechargeable Emergency Light

for anyone having problems getting the lags in that are on the upper side of the bottom bracket. mount the top section of the pull bar first. drill your pilot holes in the correct location for the bottom brackets. once you've done this, hand thread in your lag bolt with the bracket free. tighten the bolt down almost all the way then reattach the top of the pull up bar to the support bracket with the supplied bolts. you might have to flex the upper section to align the bolt holes. if you don't do this you'll have to angle the lag bolts in.

I had both my 2 sons on this and myself and it's holding strong. roughly 300lbs. My wife has said the bar is smaller diameter than our current pull up bar. I don't think it'll be an issue. text_fidelity_a:
Wise Owl Outfitters Camping Towel - Camping Accessories, Quick Dry Microfiber Towel for Travel, Hiking, Yoga, Workout, and Backpacking *UPDATED REVIEW*: In my initial review I loved the towels and only docked a star because the colors were off slightly. I'm now down to 1 star and feeling disappointed for trying to support a lesser-known American brand. I should've just gone with a more affordable option like Walmart for a no-name towel....

At the time I received my towels I didn't notice they were two different styles, we didn't unpackage them and they came in identical carry sacks. I realized when we used them together this weekend they are different. His towel has rounded edges and a soft fabric tag. My towel set has a cheaper-feeling paper tag and square edges. Again, these aren't make-or-break issues for a camp towel but I literally bought two of the SAME THING at the SAME time - it's not like I bought one last year and a newer style replaced the old one. Why couldn't you just send me two of the same thing? And why do none of the photos show a rounded edged towel?

UGHHHH. I've come away feeling like this company is not all it's cracked up to be and the products are misrepresented. It's a shame!!! I repped Wise Owl hard and bragged to many of my climbing/outdoorsy friends that I found an affordable and cool start-up. I've purchased Wise Owl towels, a camp pillow, a camp blanket, and was gifted their hammock. I feel like I know the products well and I'm sad to say I won't recommend some of them.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I'm an avid camper and climber. I found out about Wise Owl after receiving a hammock as a gift (it's awesome btw). I decided to try these towels to save some space in our packs (my partner and I have been lugging around standard bath towels). I purchased the Red set in XL and gifted him the Marine Blue set in XL. We are camping this weekend so I decided to take my towel out of the bag for a test run.

Pros - Comes in a carry sack that packs easily. ​Just as absorbent as my regular towel, soft, and large enough to dry me off completely including my hair. I could probably get by with the Large size if I wanted to save even more space. The snap loop will be nice to use to rig the towel up on a tree branch without getting tree bits all over the towel.

Cons - **IF COLOR IS IMPORTANT TO YOU: The Red is much more like the Orange listing. Easy to see in my orangey-coral bathroom. The Marine Blue is not Aqua either as the listing shows, but much more like the one listed as Royal Blue (no pics because my partner took his home with him). Both have the correct tags attached so I know I didn't get the wrong items. A little disappointing because I was attempting to color coordinate gear so I knocked a star off for that.
text_fidelity_b: Wise Owl Outfitters Camping Towel - Camping Accessories, Quick Dry Microfiber Towel for Travel, Hiking, Yoga, Workout, and Backpacking

text_fidelity_a:
Altus Athletic 3lb. Fitness Hoops Based on the other reviews, I expected to be extremely disappointed in this Altus Fitness Hoop. However, I absolutely adore this product because assembly is easy (see ASSEMBLY CAUTION note below) and since the hoop is weighted it is easy to keep going while doing the regular "hula hoop" motion. The hoop also has an all foam exterior so it cushions the impact on your mid-section.

I was able to do the traditional core excercise for 20 minutes straight without a problem. The only issue I had was that my mid-section felt sore because of the constant weight that was rotating around my stomach and waist. (The instructions warn of this for first time users.)

The hoop is a bit large and you have to use all the alternating color segments when assembling, so you can't make it smaller. It is about about 2-3 inches larger in circumference than my regular adult hula hoop which fit snugly inside the circumference of this hoop. As a result, I had to use this in the parking lot of my condo complex because I had no room in the house. This resulted in some spectators, of course.

Besides doing my core exercise in public, I also tried to do the arm exercises with the hoop. However, due to the weight I was unable to; but then again I never used a hula hoop any other way other than on my hips and that is all I wanted this for.

Other than the soreness I felt due to the rotating weight, this hoop is lots of fun. I can't vouch for the claim that it will imporve core strength and trim your waist, but I suppose that it might if you do it longer enough over a couple of months. When I hula my movement is very subtle so I doubt I'm burning more than a few calories. However, if you really gyrate when you hula, then you'll get more of a workout with this device.

ASSEMBLY CAUTION: The assembly instructions that came with this product are extremely poor. The way to assemble this hoop so that it does not come apart is to insert each segment into the previous segment and make sure that the "segment's release button" for each segment on your RIGHT is slightly protruding under the foam where the button connector dots are located for each segment on the LEFT. To test, twist (in an up and down motion) the left and right segments you just connected and also try to pull the segments in the opposite direction. If neither segment twists or pulls apart, then they are securely connected. Repeat this procedure for each segment of the hoop. Not once did this hoop fall apart on me. However, had I not done the twist and pull test, it would have fallen apart repeatedly because it takes some finagling to get each segment in place securely. Although this hoop is easy to assemble it still took me about 10-15 minutes to assemble the entire hoop since I made about 4 attempts and 4 tests per left and right segment to get the segments securely connected so they wouldn't fall off no matter how hard I pulled or twisted.

May 14 Update: I've been using this hoop every day except one for over a week now and still love it. It has not come apart once. Due to the weight of the hoop hitting against my body on rotation, I did develop a one inch bruise on my right hip. Other than this brusie I don't have any negative effects and the soreness I experienced when I used it the first time has gone away completely. I absolutely love this fitness hula hoop. Although I don't think I'm losing any weight from this, I find it a lot of fun and it's worth it just for that. One caveat - if you have cats (or dogs), don't leave the hoop where they can reach it. I put mine by the door a few minutes before I went out with it and my cats chewed through the soft foam on one segment of the hoop. The foam is easily destructible.
text_fidelity_b: Altus Athletic 3lb. Fitness Hoops

text_fidelity_a: Intech Golf Swing Impact Bag This impact bag measures 16 inches in diameter and 10 inches tall. It appears to be made of a very durable coated fabric that seems that it would stand up to a lot of use. It has a nylon strap-type handle on the top, under which lies the zipper that is used to install the towels or other soft materials that can be used to fill the bag for use. There is a plastic anchor loop on the bottom that could be used to anchor it to something solid to keep from having to consistently have to chase it after striking it. Now, I must admit that I am an intermediate golfer at best. With that, my main takeaways from using the bag is that it provides a durable, soft impact surface that can be used to swing a club and just practice the swing for purposes such as loosening up after injury, etc. While you could conceivably feel an open or closed club face at impact, I’m not that certain that there is a tremendous amount of actual feedback value that could be gained in reference to the swing. I certainly wouldn’t agree with the promo statement “Use at home to provide same quality practice time as hitting countless balls at the range”. There is also the issue of the noise. If used outside, especially in a fairly populated area, the loud noise that it makes at impact could certainly irritate neighbors. If used inside, I think you’d pretty much have to use earplugs. There may be other users that are more experienced golfers than I that might know of more valuable uses, but as for me, I’ll give it two stars.
text_fidelity_b: Intech Golf Swing Impact Bag

text_fidelity_a: Cliff Keen F5 Tornado Headgear I have two wrestlers in my house. One in middle school and the other in high school. When they both expressed an interest, I immediately thought about the "cauliflower ear" that I have seen on some wrestlers. As a mother, one of the things that I worry about is my son's health, and in this case his ears. Investing in good ear protection is a must, so I set out to find the most protective headgear on the market. We purchased this same brand of headgear for my oldest son, and he has had absolutely no problems with it. According to my son, the Cliff Keen F5 Tornado Headgear is comfortable and he definitely feels protected. He says that he doesn't feel the impact of someone grabbing his head, and that it stays firmly in place. He finds that the straps on the top and under the chin are comfortable and keep the headgear in place without making it feel too restrictive. It also doesn't interfere with his hearing. We did not use in rain but should do ok in light rain or bring a tarp for extra protection in windy downpours. The “rainfly” is just a very small cover for the small opening at the top. But I sprayed the tent with water and did not leak.
Zippered bug net doors worked well and the main solid doors have tie backs.

So what are the cons at this price range? Zippers: very cheap plastic....would suggest being very careful. Thickness of tent: would not place on rough areas or use roughly, always use ground tarp. Size: Best for a person near 5’ even though it is 6.5’ in measurement. I’m 6’1” and I had to position from corner to corner to not have the tent side in my face and doesn’t work well with rectangle sleeping bags or bag mats.

Overall, I was very surprised and would buy again. The pros and value far outweigh the cons. Our other tents and hammocks cost a whole lot more. So if you are worried about durability, buy two. Still less than most basic tents and is super light and small when in the bag.

text_fidelity_a:
MSR WhisperLite International Compact Multi-fuel Camping and Backpacking Stove I've had this stove for twenty years. I really like what I've done with the stove, and all the amazing exploits I've had with it might cause me to reminisce fondly of it, but the fact is it leaves a lot to be desired. Yes, it worked to melt snow at extreme altitudes. Yes it worked as nearly my entire kitchen on multi-week treks in the backcountry. Yes, it survived 20 years and still works dependably, sort of.

I can only remember being well and truly frustrated with it one time, on backcountry ski trip. It was storming outside the tent, and I was at high altitude. I only filled the bottle with about an inch and a half of fuel because it was only an overnighter. The bloody thing would not stay lit. After that, I bought a smaller bottle to avoid problems with a low fuel level. I also bought a larger bottle for multi-week trips.

This is a stove that rarely works at its best. Most of the time it manages to work acceptably. Some of the time it works poorly. It was rare that it worked truly bad.

I always used white gas in it. It's fairly efficient so I never had an experience where I ran out of fuel, or if I did, it was inconsequential because it was on the last day or something. I'd be more concerned with running out of isobutane with one of those systems.

This stove system is both finnicky and fragile. It really works well if the stove is in just the right condition, with the bottle filled just the right amount, the stove level, the bottle at the proper angle for the pick-up tube, and at the right pressure.

Despite the stove itself being very tough, the plastic bottle valve doesn't stand up. The replacements are expensive, and the reviews for that replacement show a consensus that these things have problems. I would say the reviews for those replacement pumps are probably more accurate and unbiased than the ones for the stove.

I have a MSR Reactor for a couple years now. It simply blows the Whisperlite away in terms of melting snow or boiling water. It's far simpler, almost stupid-proof, way faster, and practically just as light and compact when you factor the fuel bottle and pot.

More recently, I acquired a Trangia alcohol stove. As a minimalist with a preference for ultralight style, it was appealing. I don't have extensive experience with it yet. I bought it to simmer and cook, which the Whisperlite and Reactor don't do well at all. While the Trangia would be slower to melt snow or boil water (the forte of the Reactor, and Whisperlite), I believe it would still do the job under practically all the conditions I'll encounter. Alcohol is a far more appealing fuel to carry than white gas or isobutane.

At this point, I have a broken bottle valve. It works, but the plastic clips to retain the pump plunger are broken. For less than the price of a replacement part, I acquired the Trangia stove that I will likely use for the next 20 years. It's lighter, cleaner, easier to use, simmers nicely, and takes less space in the pack.
text_fidelity_b: MSR WhisperLite International Compact Multi-fuel Camping and Backpacking Stove
